---
title: "Data security"
subtitle: "What's safe to share with Gemini, and why your account matters. About 5 minutes to read."
---

Before you share any data with an AI tool, check three things. Which account are you signed in with? How sensitive
is the data? And does anyone you got it from limit how it can be shared?

## 1. Your account {#account}

With your NC State account, Gemini is on NC State's
[list of approved AI tools]({{< var security.approved-list >}}). The list says to use gemini.google.com "and log in
with your NC State account", and it rejects the free public version for university data. That's the version you get
with a personal Google account.

Under NC State's agreement with Google, your chats and uploaded files "won't be reviewed by human reviewers or
otherwise used to improve generative AI models" ([Google's education FAQ]({{< var security.google-faq >}})). Gemini
says the same when you first open it, and adds that your Gemini Activity can't be turned off. Your chats are kept,
so think before you paste.

**To check:** at the bottom left of Gemini, your name should have **Edu** under it.

## 2. How sensitive is the data? {#levels}

NC State's [Data Management Framework]({{< var security.framework >}}) sorts university data into four levels.

| Level | What it means | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Purple**, ultra-sensitive | Disclosure or loss poses the highest risk | Social Security numbers, passwords, encryption keys, biometrics |
| **Red**, highly sensitive | A high risk | Driver's license and passport numbers, mother's maiden name, immigration numbers |
| **Yellow**, moderately sensitive | A moderate to low risk | Date of birth, race, gender, transcripts |
| **Green**, not sensitive | A low risk; it may be disclosed to anyone | Data that's already public, like this session's practice data |

Data that nobody has classified must be treated as at least yellow until it is. The data's steward sets the level;
for research data, ask your PI first.

**Gemini, with your NC State login, is approved for data up to red. Never purple.**

## 3. Agreements come first {#agreements}

A tool being approved doesn't cancel what an agreement says about the data. These are the ones textile researchers
meet most:

- **An industry partner's data under a nondisclosure agreement,** like production reports, recipes or test results.
  The practice data is exactly this kind of report; its factory chose to publish it.
- **Sponsored research,** where the sponsor's terms can limit who processes the data.
- **Human-subjects data,** such as surveys, interviews or fit studies. Your IRB protocol and consent form say where
  the data may go.
- **A data use agreement** for data you got from another institution or company.
- **Export-controlled** technical data.

If an agreement limits sharing, or you're not sure, don't upload. Ask the PI, or whoever signed the agreement, first.
When NC State's approved list and an agreement disagree, follow whichever is stricter.

## 4. Describe it instead of uploading {#describe}

You can get Gemini's help without sharing a single row. Describe the data's layout, paste the header row and a few
made-up rows of the same kind, and ask for formulas, pivot-table steps or chart steps. You run them in your own
sheet, so the data never leaves it. The [Explore](explore.qmd#describe) page practices this.

This works for any data you're allowed to keep in your NC State Google Drive. If an agreement doesn't allow even
that, ask before you use any cloud tool.

Column names can be sensitive too, like a partner's product codes, so rename them before you paste. A list of the
distinct values in a column, from a formula like `=SORT(UNIQUE(G2:G))`, is often fine to share when the rows aren't.
Check that it doesn't reveal anything first.

## 5. The decision guide {#guide}

{{< include _decision-guide.md >}}

::: {.decision-words}
1. **Signed in with a personal Google account?** Switch to your NC State account. The free public Gemini isn't
   approved for university data.
2. **Is any of it purple** (Social Security numbers, passwords, keys, biometrics)? Don't put it in any AI tool.
3. **Could an agreement limit sharing** (IRB protocol, data use agreement, partner NDA, sponsor terms, export
   control)? Describe it only, with headers and made-up rows, and ask whoever signed the agreement first.
4. **Otherwise,** for green, yellow or red data that nothing limits, you may upload it or describe it. If you upload,
   include only the columns you need.
:::

you'd do with data you can't share.
